content:
ashley: heads up — canary push for `web-service:v2026-03-21` got skipped by deploy-bot. seeing a tag prefix collision in ECR.

deploy-bot: publish-blocked: tag `web-service:staging-20260321` already exists and points to a different digest. provenance attestation mismatch (cosign). 

ashley: I triggered the build twice in CI (flaky runner), looks like two different build digests ended up with the same human-readable prefix. oof.

matt: can you paste the ECR image URIs/digests?

ashley: sure — `account.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/web-service@sha256:abcd1234...` and the conflicting one is `...@sha256:efgh5678...`. both attempted to be published as `staging-20260321`.

jen: is this a provenance/attestation failure or just a tag collision? deploy-bot message said cosign / attestation mismatch.

ashley: deploy-bot refused the publish because the existing `staging-20260321` attestation's buildmetadata didn't match. system policy: we never overwrite a tag with a different provenance.

matt: that is the intended safety behaviour. how urgent is the canary? are we inside the release window?

release-manager: release window is open for another 2h. canary needed before 2pm PT to hit the promo cutoff.

ashley: we have two options: 1) retag the desired digest to a fresh ephemeral canary tag (e.g. `staging-ephemeral-4129`) and proceed; 2) revert the CI push that created the conflicting image and attempt republish with corrected metadata (slower).

sre-oncall: option 1 seems safest to unblock canary quickly. but we need to pin the digest everywhere and update the release notes to reference the digest, not the human tag. also add a follow-up to fix the CI tag-prefix collision.

matt: +1 for ephemeral tag and pin. Also we should avoid human date-based tags for automated builds — they collide when retrying. we should change the CI to append the build id.

ashley: I'll retag and push: `aws ecr put-image --repository-name web-service --image-tag staging-ephemeral-4129 --image-manifest $(aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name web-service --image-ids imageDigest=sha256:abcd1234 --query images[0].imageManifest --output text)`

deploy-bot: note: deploy automation requires an attestation record. if you retag manually we will still block promote unless provenance is attached or the digest is pinned in the canary route config.

ashley: understood. I'll update the canary route to pin to `sha256:abcd1234...` instead of relying on tag. posting to release notes: "Canary uses image digest sha256:abcd1234 (staging-ephemeral-4129)."

release-manager: please also add a short blurb in release notes about why the original `staging-20260321` was not used (provenance mismatch) so downstream teams don't get confused.

jen: ops checklist: 1) retag to ephemeral (ashley) 2) pin canary route to digest (ashley) 3) run canary smoke tests (matt) 4) update release notes + open CI bug (release-manager)

ashley: done with retag and route pin. kicked canary deploy.

matt: running smoke now. looks good so far — latency and error rates normal. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded: route `web-service.canary` pinned to digest sha256:abcd1234. promotion eligible.

release-manager: great. publish release notes update to docs now and schedule CI fix for next sprint.

ashley: opened GH issue for CI tag policy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-ci/issues/142 — title: "avoid date-only tags; append build id to prevent prefix collisions"

sre-oncall: follow-up: audit recent pushes with date-based tags and ensure no other conflicts (I'll run a script).

matt: good catch. closing thread once release notes are updated.

ashley: release notes updated with digest + explanation. closing unless anyone objects.

jen: thanks everyone. lesson: for now, always pin by digest for production promotions.

ashley: closing. :lock:
